title: Junior and senior Young Men Olympians; Clark's own membership
summary: Clark explains the junior branch, joined as a boy of seven, and his return from Chicago to the older branch.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: What about the young men, Olympians, the junior branch? That's related to the older ones?
Old men. They set up under that. They set up under us.
I was in the juniors when I was a boy.
So the one, do they go from one to the other when they get older?

Well you can. You can't switch. You see, I was in the junior when I was a boy. I was a boy about seven years old. And I stayed in that thing, I don't know, I guess I was about 13 to 14 years old and I got out. Then I went to Chicago and I stayed in Chicago for about six years. And when I came back, well I wanted to get back in, so I said, well I ain't going back in. The kids, we call them the kids. And I went on to the old men. And I've been in the old men ever since.
